newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch demand Turkmen explanation on asylum flight.
newsitem.headline: Dutch demand Turkmen explanation on asylum flight.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Tuesday it had grounded a Turkmenistan Airlines plane until the Turkmen aviation authorities explained why it had been allowed to make an unauthorised flight to the Netherlands.

"We have asked the aviation authorities and the airline how it can have been allowed to happen that this plane was permitted to take off for Amsterdam without clearance," a transport ministry spokeswoman said.
She said the plane would not be allowed to leave until the authorities had responded.
The flight with 173 Sri Lankan Tamils on board was allowed to touch down at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport on Sunday after the pilot signalled he was running out of fuel.
All the passengers on board subsequently applied for political asylum and will be allowed to stay in reception centres in the Netherlands while their requests are processed.
The Dutch courts have stipulated that anyone from Sri Lanka who applies for asylum is entitled to a full hearing process, which can take years to complete.

The Sri Lankan government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in a 14-year war for independence by minority Tamils in the north and east of the island. Tamil groups say the toll is much higher.
The flight was thought to have taken off from the Turkmen capital Ashgabat, the ministry spokeswoman said.
